problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
{y}^{′}+3y=6{e}^{-3x}+10{e}^{2x},
$$

has the complementary solution ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{-3x}$, find the particular solution to the equation.

${y}_{p}(x)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

We see that the right-hand side is $6{e}^{-3x}+10{e}^{2x},$ and ${e}^{-3x}$ is a term in the complementary solution, while ${e}^{2x}$ is not, so we assume that a particular solution takes the form 

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha x{e}^{-3x}+\beta {e}^{2x},
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined.

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & =(\alpha x{e}^{-3x}+\beta {e}^{2x})^{′} \\  & =\alpha (x{e}^{-3x})^{′}+\beta ({e}^{2x})^{′} \\  & =\alpha ({e}^{-3x}-3x{e}^{-3x})+2\beta {e}^{2x} \\  & =\alpha (1-3x){e}^{-3x}+2\beta {e}^{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\alpha (1-3x){e}^{-3x}+2\beta {e}^{2x})+3(\alpha x{e}^{-3x}+\beta {e}^{2x}) & =6{e}^{-3x}+10{e}^{2x} \\ (1-3x+3x)\alpha {e}^{-3x}+(2\beta +3\beta ){e}^{2x} & =6{e}^{-3x}+10{e}^{2x} \\ \alpha {e}^{-3x}+5\beta {e}^{2x} & =6{e}^{-3x}+10{e}^{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients of ${e}^{-3x}$ and ${e}^{2x}$ gives

$$
\alpha =6\,\text{and}\,5\beta =10,
$$

so, we have

$$
\alpha =6\,\text{and}\,\beta =2.
$$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=6x{e}^{-3x}+2{e}^{2x}.
$$
